effects: The ETH attached to the call (msg.value) leaves the signer and the portal forwards it to the ETHYieldManager.
The same amount is minted on Blast to the signer's L2 address, or to its aliased address when the caller is a contract.
_value ETH moves on Blast from that L2 address to _to. Any part above msg.value comes from the signer's existing Blast balance.
_data runs on Blast as a call from that L2 address to _to, using _gasLimit gas paid for by burning L1 gas.
The call reverts when _to is the L2 Blast bridge and the caller is not the L1 Blast bridge. The wallet refuses _isCreation = true.
formats.shown: Deposit {msg.value} to Blast and send {_value} on L2 to {_to}, with the gas limit, the decoded L2 call and a note about aliased addresses for contract wallets.

findings.title: depositTransaction: the screen does not say that _value above msg.value comes from the signer's Blast balance.
findings.evidence: OptimismPortal.sol depositTransaction: opaqueData = abi.encodePacked(msg.value, _value, ...): mint and L2 value are separate. Descriptor interpolatedIntent 'Deposit {@.value} to Blast and send {_value} on L2 to {_to}'. Case 1 shows 'Deposit 0 ETH ... send 0.000006133436085086 ETH on L2', and the blind reader believed 'Up to 0.000006133436085086 ETH to the Blast bridge (L1 contract)' would leave the L1 wallet.
findings.fix: Say where the L2 amount comes from, e.g. 'Deposit {@.value} to Blast and send {_value} from your Blast balance to {_to}', or relabel _value as 'ETH Sent on L2 (from your Blast balance)'.

findings.title: depositTransaction: the intent 'Deposit ETH to Blast' is also shown for zero-value forced L2 calls, such as withdrawals.
findings.evidence: Case 10: intent 'Deposit ETH to Blast' with Deposit Amount 0 ETH. The nested L2 call is 'Start ETH withdrawal to Ethereum'. Descriptor intent 'Deposit ETH to Blast'.
findings.fix: Use a neutral intent such as 'Send transaction to Blast'. The interpolated sentence already carries the amounts.

findings.title: depositTransaction: the nested L2 call uses the L1 sender as @.from, but contract wallets act from an aliased address.
findings.evidence: OptimismPortal.sol depositTransaction: 'if (msg.sender != tx.origin) from = AddressAliasHelper.applyL1ToL2Alias(msg.sender)'. Descriptor _data params 'spenderPath': '@.from'. The static Note field explains the aliasing.
findings.fix: ERC-7730 cannot compute the alias. Keep the Note.

cases.notes: No L1 movement (value 0). The L2 transfer of _value comes from the signer's Blast balance. The reader wrongly thought it would leave L1.
No L1 movement. The nested L2 call starts a withdrawal, and the reader understood it.

formats.key: finalizeWithdrawalTransaction(uint256 hintId,(uint256 nonce,address sender,address target,uint256 value,uint256 gasLimit,bytes data) _tx)
effects: Marks the proven withdrawal _tx as finalized so it cannot be replayed.
Claims the ETH for the withdrawal from the ETHYieldManager (request from proving, hintId) and sends the amount actually received, which can be below _tx.value, to _tx.target.
Calls _tx.target with _tx.data and at least _tx.gasLimit gas, with l2Sender set to _tx.sender. Through the messenger and bridge this can pay ETH or tokens to the final recipient.
If the call to the target fails, the withdrawal still counts as finalized and is not retried.
formats.shown: Finalize withdrawal of up to {_tx.value} from {_tx.sender} to {_tx.target}, with the decoded L1 call, which shows the final payee and amount.

findings.title: finalizeWithdrawalTransaction: for bridge withdrawals the sentence names the messengers, and the real payee is two calls deep.
findings.evidence: Cases 4, 7, 8: interpolatedIntent '... from L2CrossDomainMessenger to L1CrossDomainMessenger'. The payee and amount ('Pay up to 1.088 ETH ... to 0x9578...') are only in the nested L1 Call.
findings.fix: Nothing at this level can name the inner payee. The nested descriptors show it.

findings.title: finalizeWithdrawalTransaction: a failed target call still finalizes the withdrawal, and the screen does not mention it.
findings.evidence: OptimismPortal.sol finalizeWithdrawalTransaction: 'finalizedWithdrawals[withdrawalHash] = true;' before 'SafeCall.callWithMinGas(...)'. It only reverts on failure when tx.origin == ESTIMATION_ADDRESS.
findings.fix: Optionally add a note that a withdrawal whose L1 call fails cannot be replayed through the portal.

cases.notes: A relayer finalized the withdrawal. 0.0000349 ETH went to 0x01eD..., which matches the screen.
0.00105 ETH arrived at the signer, matching the nested 'Pay up to 0.00105 ETH ... to 0x6F67...'.
No movement. A DAI claim was queued, as shown nested.
1.088 ETH arrived at the signer, as shown.
110000 BLAST was minted to the signer, matching the nested 'Pay 110000 BLAST ... to 0x6B69...'.

formats.key: proveWithdrawalTransaction((uint256 nonce,address sender,address target,uint256 value,uint256 gasLimit,bytes data) _tx,uint256 _l2OutputIndex,(bytes32 version,bytes32 stateRoot,bytes32 messagePasserStorageRoot,bytes32 latestBlockhash) _outputRootProof,bytes[] _withdrawalProof)
effects: Checks the withdrawal against the L2 output root and records it as proven at the current time. This starts the finalization wait.
On the first proof of a withdrawal with value, it asks the ETHYieldManager for a withdrawal of _tx.value. The payout to _tx.target happens later, at finalization.
No assets of the signer move. The signer pays only gas.
formats.shown: Prove withdrawal of {_tx.value} from {_tx.sender} to {_tx.target}, with the decoded call that will run at finalization. The proof data is hidden.

findings.title: proveWithdrawalTransaction: the sentence states an exact amount, but the later payout can be lower.
findings.evidence: OptimismPortal.sol finalizeWithdrawalTransaction: 'txValueWithDiscount = address(this).balance - etherBalance'. Descriptor interpolatedIntent 'Prove withdrawal of {_tx.value} ...'. The field label 'Requested Amount' and the finalize sentence 'up to' already hint at this.
findings.fix: Optionally write 'Prove withdrawal of up to {_tx.value} ...'.

cases.notes: No movement. A relayer proved someone else's withdrawal, as shown.

couldNotCheck: ETHYieldManager (portal.yieldManager()) is not in the directory. Its claimWithdrawal sets how much ETH finalizeWithdrawalTransaction sends to _tx.target, and its requestWithdrawal is called by proveWithdrawalTransaction. Without its source, the bound shown as 'up to _tx.value' cannot be confirmed from code. The mined cases paid the full amount.
